(a) Preapplication review. A pre-application conference is intended to assist both the city and the applicant with regard to what type of application of record will be required for the proposed development activity. It also provides a means of exchanging information about the application process and how to develop land in conformance with the requirements and standards of this chapter. All pre-application conferences shall be governed by the following procedures:
(1) Voluntary and required preapplication conferences. There are two types of pre-application conferences, one type which is voluntary, and another which is required. They are distinguished as follows. No administrative or formal application or submissions are required to initiate a preapplication conference.
a. Voluntary. A voluntary pre-application conference may be arranged between the applicant and the building inspector or city manager's designee for minor subdivisions, minor lot-line adjustments or re-combinations of previously plat/planted lots.
b. Required. A pre-application conference shall be required between the applicant and building inspector and the city manager's designee for all major subdivisions.
(2) Scope of consultation. Any discussions and recommendations that result from either type of pre-application conference shall be non-binding on the applicant and the city. Whenever a subdivision within the jurisdiction of the building inspector or the city manager's designee is proposed, the applicant may, at his discretion, consult early and informally with the building inspector or the city manager's designee for advice and assistance. The applicant may submit sketches and data, or a conceptual layout showing existing conditions within the site and in its vicinity and the proposed layout of the development. If the tract of land is not to be initially subdivided in its entirety, the applicant shall provide sketches for the entire tract and indicate the proposed unit division of phased development boundaries.
(3) Recommendations. Should the applicant request a pre-application conference, the building inspector or the city manager's designee shall return any submitted sketch plans as quickly as possible and inform the applicant of areas where the proposed plans do not comply with the requirements set forth in these regulations. However, in no instance shall the pre-application conference be made or accepted in lieu of the required plat/plans and specifications contained herein.
(b) Administrative applications. Administrative applications may be submitted for a recombination of previously platted/planned lots, or minor lot line adjustments. The building inspector or the city manager's designee shall approve, disapprove, or otherwise reconcile administrative applications. The decision to approve an administrative application by the building inspector or the city manager's designee shall be made after consideration of all the relevant facts before him. Such relevant facts shall be measured to determine compliance with this chapter. The review procedures for an administrative application are as follows:
(1) Approval. If the proposed recombination of previously platted/planned lots, or minor lot line adjustment as set forth in the application is in compliance with this chapter the lot recombination, or lot line adjustment shall then be recorded at the county clerk of court office. Final approval will be withheld pending confirmation to the city from the clerk of courts that the plat/plan has been filed.
(2) Disapproval. If the proposal submitted is not approved or otherwise reconciled, the reason for disapproval shall be stated in writing on the application.
(3) Reconciliation. Any administrative application that has been formally disapproved or deemed incomplete or deficient by the building inspector or the city manager's designee may be resubmitted for proper reconciliation. An additional application fee shall not be necessary for a re-submission.
(4) Review deadline. The building inspector or the city manager's designee shall issue a final determination regarding an administrative application within 30 days of the date that the application is complete and formally accepted by the building inspector or the city manager's designee. Failure by the building inspector or the city manager's designee to issue a final determination within the 30-day deadline shall constitute automatic approval of the application only if the applicant receives all other required local, state and federal approvals.
(c) Formal applications. The filing of a formal application is established to allow expedient and thorough review of larger scale development projects which are more complex and require substantial review. Major subdivisions are subject to the formal application process. Review of formal applications shall be subject to the preliminary and final plat/plan procedures outlined in sections 46-43, 46-44, 46-45, 46-46, and 46-47.
(d) Coordination of review with other required local, state and federal reviews. The applicant shall be responsible for submitting applications to and receiving approval for any proposed development from other local, state and federal agencies as required by this chapter and all other applicable ordinances, regulations, and laws. At a minimum, the applicant shall submit copies of applications to such local, state and federal agencies along with the application information provided to the city. The building inspector or the city manager's designee may grant conditional approval for any municipal application upon approval by any and all local, state and federal agencies with jurisdiction to approve any aspect of the proposed development. An applicant shall not be issued a construction permit by the building inspector or the city manager's designee until such time that the applicant submits a copy of all required approvals from the applicable local, state and federal agencies.
(e) Special impact studies. During review of any application, the building inspector or the city manager's designee, or the city council may determine that additional specific technical information regarding the project and its potential environmental, fiscal or traffic impacts is needed. If such a determination is made, the building inspector or the city manager's designee or the city council may condition approval of an application upon preparation of a special impact study intended to analyze the potential impacts of the development on the specific areas of concern. Where preparation of a special impact study has been required, no application shall be approved until such study has been submitted with adequate time provided for review. The responsibility and costs for such a study shall be borne by the applicant unless the city manager's designee determines otherwise.
(f) Development construction phasing. Whenever a major subdivision is proposed, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may require construction phasing. Where it has been determined during the review of a major subdivision application that a proposed development would exhaust or exceed the available capacity of existing public facilities including, but not limited to, roads, municipal water and sewer, fire protection, schools and police protection, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may require the applicant to submit a phased development schedule that shall demonstrate consistency and concurrency with the planning and installation of adequate public infrastructure and facilities to serve the affected development.
(g) Application and review fees. Application fees for the pre-application conference, administrative applications, formal applications and plan/plat changes and modifications will be assessed at the time of filing of a preliminary plat/plan according to the schedule on file in the clerk's office. Any formal application that involves development phasing as described in this chapter shall be subject to application and review fees for each submission of a preliminary plat/plan.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)

588:
(a) Land suitability. The selection of an area for any subdivision shall be located strategically on lands that are suitable for the types of development proposed. Factors relevant to selection of an area for subdivision or planned development shall be considerate of land use related criteria stated in section 62-119. Other factors shall include, but not be limited to, the suitability of land as it relates to flooding, proper drainage, steep slopes, bedrock, topography, utility easements or other features or problems which may create unfavorable development conditions.
(b) General site design guidelines. The proposed development must be designed so as to produce an environment of stable and desirable character not out of harmony with the surrounding neighborhood. The review by the building inspector or the city manager's designee shall consider the following design elements:
(1) Privacy. Personal and individual privacy shall be maintained and balanced with the provision of public and common areas.
(2) Variety. Interest and variety shall be sought by means of street design and changes in and mixtures of building types, heights, facades, setbacks, planting, or size of open space. The design shall be harmonious as a whole and not simply from street-to-street.
(3) Traffic and parking. Through or commercial traffic shall not be encouraged within a subdivision of less than 20 acres. Proposed local or internal streets should curve to discourage the fast movement of traffic.
(c) Naming requirements.
(1) Street naming. The purpose of naming streets is to provide an orderly process for identifying geographic areas and for orienting users of the street system. Naming requirements for streets shall be observed as follows:
a. Approval. Street names and address numbers shall be subject to the approval of the building inspector or the city manager's designee
b. Duplication of names. Street names shall not duplicate nor be closely approximated phonetically to any name of an existing city street or road.
c. Continuity of names. Any street or road which is a continuation or an approximation or logical continuation of any existing dedicated street or road shall bear the same name.
d. Small cul-de-sacs. Small cul-de-sacs which have less than five interior lots may be omitted for name purposes when the house numbers are continuous with those of the street or road to which they have access.
e. Street name designations. Street name designations shall be used as follows:
1. Boulevard or parkway: shall be reserved for streets or roads designated on the highway classification map which are planned to have a median divider of sufficient size to allow for landscaping.
2. Avenue or road: shall be reserved for streets or roads of substantial continuity such as major or minor arterials designated on the highway classification map.
3. Street or drive: shall be reserved for streets of less continuity such as collector streets and roads as designated on the highway classification map.
4. Court, place, circle, way or terrace: shall be reserved for streets and/or roads with no continuity.
(2) Name of subdivision. Any proposed name for a subdivision development shall not duplicate, or too closely approximate phonetically, the name of any other subdivision. The building inspector or the city manager's designee shall have final authority to designate the name of a subdivision which shall be determined upon acceptance of the concept plan.
(d) Access.
(1) Intent. All subdivisions shall provide adequate public access for street, utility, and pedestrian systems which shall be designed and constructed to facilitate efficient movement and circulation to ease congestion and to promote safety.
(2) Design standards. Where a major subdivision borders on or contains an existing or proposed primary arterial, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may require that access to such streets be limited by one of the following means:
a. Subdivided lots bordering a primary arterial shall back onto the primary arterial and front onto a parallel local street. No access to these types of lots shall be provided from the primary arterial, and screening in the form of a buffer or screen shall be provided in a strip of land along the rear property line of such lots.
b. Where there exists a marginal access or service road separated from the primary arterial, a planting or a grass strip shall be established and maintained and there shall be access thereto at appropriate points.
c. When the development has 75 or more lots then it shall have at least two entrances from a public street that are at least 200 feet apart (as measured from centerline to centerline along the intersecting street line). The building inspector or the city manager's designee may require additional access as it deems necessary to accommodate safe entrance, egress, and emergency access to the development, and for the purpose of accommodating emergency, rescue, or other critical public safety vehicles.
(e) Comprehensive plan consistency. All subdivisions, and those requirements and standards that apply are intended to serve as a device to further the goals, objectives and policies of the comprehensive plan. The review of a subdivision provides a comprehensive means of addressing a wide range of issues for a broad geographic area. The use of a theme or development concept will provide a basis for relating the proposed development request to standards provided for in all municipal land development regulations and the comprehensive plan. The policies of the comprehensive plan's land use element, including the future land use map, in conjunction with the preceding policies of other comprehensive plan elements, shall form the basis for reviewing proposed subdivisions.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
589:
All new streets constructed as a result of a subdivision shall conform to the following standards:
(1) Topography and arrangement. Roads shall be related appropriately to the topography. Grades of streets shall conform as closely as possible to the original topography. A combination of steep grades (12 percent or greater) and curves shall be avoided. All streets shall be properly integrated with the existing county road and street system. The use of curvilinear streets, or U-shaped streets shall be encouraged where such use shall result in a more desirable layout.
(2) Existing streets. Existing streets shall be continued at the same or greater width, but in no case less than the required width.
(3) Frontage on improved roads. No subdivision shall be approved unless the area to be developed shall have frontage on and access from an existing dedicated public street or road.
(4) Reserve strips. The creation of reserve strips shall not be permitted adjacent to a proposed street in such a manner to deny access from adjacent property to such street.
(5) Street jogs. Street jogs with centerline offsets of less than 200 feet shall not be permitted, unless the intersected street has separated dual lanes without median breaks at either intersection.
(6) Grading and improvement plan. Roads shall be graded and improved and shall conform to local construction standards and specifications, and shall be approved as to design and specifications in accordance with appropriate plat/plan approval.
(7) Intersections. Unless otherwise noted, required distances between streets shall be measured from centerline-to-centerline. The following standards shall also apply:
a. Streets shall be laid out to intersect as nearly as possible at right angles. A proposed new intersection of two new streets at an angle of less than 75 degrees shall not be acceptable. An oblique street shall be curved approaching an intersection and shall be approximately at right angles for at least 100 feet from the end of the curve to the street intersection. Not more than two streets shall intersect at any one point, unless specifically approved by the building inspector or the city manager's designee.
b. Proposed new intersections along one side of an existing street shall coincide with any existing intersections on the opposite side of such street. Where streets intersect major streets, their alignments shall be continuous. Intersection of major streets shall be at least 800 feet apart.
c. Minimum curb radius at the intersection of two local streets shall be at least 25 feet; and minimum curb radius at an intersection involving a collector or arterial street shall be at least 25 feet.
d. Intersections shall be designed at a flat grade wherever practical. In hilly or rolling areas, at the approach to an intersection, a leveling area shall be provided having not greater than two percent rate at a distance of 60 feet, measured from the nearest right-of-way line of the intersecting street.
e. In a corner lot, there shall be no obstruction to vision between the height of three feet and ten feet above the average grade of each street within the triangular area formed by the intersection of two road rights-of-way and a line joining them at points 25 feet away from their intersection.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)

The length and design of a cul-de-sac shall be as follows:
(1) Permanent. A permanent cul-de-sac shall serve no more than 12 families and not exceed 800 feet in length
(2) Temporary. A temporary cul-de-sac which extends for a distance greater than 200 feet shall be provided with a temporary turnaround having a diameter of 80 feet. A temporary cul-de-sac shall be allowed during phased construction of a residential subdivision. The temporary cul-de-sac must be removed before acceptance of the final plat.

594:
Paving requirements: All streets must be prepared and paved according to the following methods or by equivalent methods that are acceptable to the governing authority:
(1) Subgrade. The subgrade shall be 24 inches of compacted subgrade material compacted to 95 percent modified proctor density.
(2) Base. The base shall consist of a graded aggregate base course screened one and one half inches or smaller with a thickness of six inches after being thoroughly compacted and constructed.
a. All materials shall be secured from an approved source and shall conform to the Georgia Department of Transportation's minimum acceptable standards for this area.
b. As soon as the base material has been spread and mixed, the base shall be brought to approximate line, grade and cross-section and then rolled until the roller walks out and finally with a pneumatic tire or general-purpose roller until full thickness of the base course has been compacted thoroughly. Defects shall be remedied as soon as they are discovered. New materials shall be added if necessary and defective portions shall be entirely removed.
c. The base course shall be maintained under traffic and kept free from ruts, ridges and dusting, true to grade and cross-section until it is primed.
d. No base material shall be deposited or shaped when the subgrade is frozen or thawing or during unfavorable weather conditions.
(3) Binder course. The Binder course shall consist of fine and course aggregate and mineral filler uniformly mixed with hot mix asphalt cement in an approved mixing plant. The job mix shall be of the following type: 19.5 mm Superpave and the following thickness: two inches, and shall conform to the Department of Transportation, State of Georgia, Standard Specifications, current edition.
(4) Surface course. The surface course shall consist of fine and course aggregate and mineral filler uniformly mixed with hot mix asphalt cement in an approved mixing plant. The job mix shall be of the following type: 9.5 mm Superpave, and the following thickness: one and one-half inch and shall conform to the Department of Transportation, State of Georgia, Standard Specification, current edition. 12.5 superpave mix may be allowed with approval from the city manager.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
597:
Block design shall conform to sound design principles and the length, width and the shape shall be determined with due regard to:
(1) Zoning district requirements as to lot size.
(2) Topographic conditions.
(3) Need for safe, convenient access and traffic circulation.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)

599:
The size, shape, and orientation of lots shall be appropriate to the proposed subdivision and shall conform to the development standards for the applicable zoning district. Other standards shall include the following:
(1) No lot shall be subdivided by a city or county boundary.
(2) Every lot shall abut a street.
(3) Where parcels of land are subdivided into unusually large lots, such parcels shall be arranged to allow for the opening of future streets and logical further subdivision.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
600:
(a) The applicant shall place permanent boundary markers or monuments for reference in any subdivision as required herein, and as approved by a registered land surveyor.
(b) Monuments shall be located on street right-of-way lines, at street intersections, angle points of curves and lot corners. They shall be spaced to be within sight distance of each other, the sight lines being wholly contained within the street limits.
(c) The external boundaries of a subdivision shall be monumented in the field by monuments of stone or concrete, not less than 30 inches in length, not less than four inches square or five inches in diameter, and marked on top with a cross, brass plug, iron rod, or other durable material securely embedded; or by iron rods or pipes at least 30 inches long and two inches in diameter. These monuments shall be placed not more than 1,400 feet apart in any straight line and at all corners, at the end of all curves, at the point where a curve changes its radius, at all angle points in any line, and at all angle points along the meander line, said points to be not less than 20 feet back from the bank of any river or stream, except that when such corners or points fall within a street, or proposed future street, the monuments shall be placed in the side line of the street.
(d) All internal boundaries and those corners and points not referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be monumented in the field by like monuments as described above. These monuments shall be placed at all block corners, at each end of all curves, at a point where a river changes its radius, and at all angle points at any line.
(e) The lines of lots that extend to rivers or streams shall be monumented in the field by iron pipes at least 30 inches long and seven-eighths of an inch in diameter or by round or square iron bars at least 30 inches long. These monuments shall be placed at the point of intersection of the river or stream lot line, with a meander line established not less than 20 feet back from the bank of the river or stream.
(f) All monuments shall be properly set in the ground and approved by a registered land surveyor prior to the time the building inspector or the city manager's designee recommends approval of the final plan.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
606:
Prior to the approval of the final plat/plan, installation of street and utility improvements shall be made. The developer, at his own expense, shall be required to have installed street and utility improvements as required in this article.

607:
After all necessary sewer, water, and other underground utilities have been installed, the developer shall install curbs and gutters and shall surface or cause to be surfaced roadways to the widths described in this chapter. Said surfacing shall be of such character as is suitable for the expected traffic and in harmony with similar improvements in surrounding areas. Adequate provision shall be made for culverts, drains, and bridges.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
608:
Shoulders, curb, and gutters shall be installed on all streets in a subdivision. Depending on the street class a rollover curb, or six-inch curb and gutter may be used (see table below). Arterial | 6" Curb and gutter

609:
The development shall contain adequate stormwater management facilities to accommodate on-site runoff that would be generated by a 25-year storm event. The building inspector or the city manager's designee may request assistance from the county soil conservation district, or the city engineer in evaluating the applicant's proposed measures to comply with this requirement. Any costs associated with this evaluation assistance shall be paid by the applicant. All drainage improvements shall tie into any available or natural drainageways along the adjoining public streets. Post-development flows shall not exceed pre-development flows for the two to 25-year storm events. The 50-year storm shall pass through the detention facility with one foot of freeboard and the 100-year storm shall pass through the detention facility without over topping. The SCS method shall be utilized for detention calculations. The rational method may be used for pipe sizing.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
610:
Installation of street lights may be required in accordance with design and specifications standards recommended by the local electric public utility system; however, the compatibility with the following guidelines shall be considered in developing a street lighting plan for a subdivision:
(1) Lighting for safety shall be provided at intersections, along walkways, at entryways, between buildings, and in parking areas.
(2) The spacing of street lights shall be equal to four times the height of the street light.
(3) The maximum height of the street light shall not exceed the maximum building height permitted, or 25 feet, whichever is less.
(4) The height and shielding of lighting standards shall provide proper lighting without hazard to drivers or nuisance to residents, and the design of lighting standards shall be of a type appropriate to the development and the community.
(5) Spotlights, if used, shall be placed on standards pointing toward the building and positioned as not to blind the residents, rather than on the buildings and directed outward which creates dark shadows adjacent to buildings.
(6) Street lights shall be pointed downward.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
611:
All proposed wire or cable utilities shall be located underground throughout any proposed subdivision. The utility must maintain five feet separation from water and sewer pipes in a dedicated utility easement.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
612:
Easements shall be provided along front lot lines for utilities (both private and public); such easements shall conform to the technical standards provided. Proper coordination shall be established between the developer and appropriate utility companies for the establishment of utility easements on properties adjoining the subdivision. Where topographical or other conditions make it impractical to place utilities on the rear lot lines, perpetual unobstructed easements at least ten feet in width shall be provided along side lot lines with satisfactory access to the road or rear lot lines. These easements shall, through deed covenants, be maintained clear of dense shrubbery, trees or fences. Permanent easements for drainage, sewer and water shall be provided for infrastructure in the right-of-way.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
613:
All subdivisions must be connected to the city water system. Water mains for both domestic use and fire protection within the development shall be properly connected with the city water system. The mains shall be constructed in such a manner as to serve adequately all lots shown on the subdivision plat/plan. The mains shall be installed in conformance with the technical standards as established by the city manager's designee. The city may incur the cost for any difference in the cost of the laying of oversized pipe and outfall systems which are needed in excess of the required water and sewer facilities needed to exclusively serve the new subdivision as determined by the public works director or the city manager's designee.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
614:

The city may incur the cost for any difference in the cost of the laying of oversized pipe and outfall systems which are needed in excess of the required water and sewer facilities needed to exclusively serve the new subdivision as determined by the public works director or the city manager's designee
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
615:

(1) R-1A residential: Both sides of road required.
(2) R-1B residential: Both sides of road required.
(3) R-1C residential: Both sides of road required.
(4) R-2 residential: Both sides of road required.
(5) R-3 residential: Both sides of road required.
(6) Other zoning districts: as required by the commission.
Unless otherwise specified, all sidewalks shall be four inches thick (six inches at driveways) with a minimum width of five feet. All sidewalks shall slope one-fourth of an inch to the foot toward the curb. All sidewalks shall be ADA compliant.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
616:
(a) All new or existing roads, public or private, which are included in a subdivision shall be furnished and installed with street name signs. All necessary traffic signs (slow, stop, caution, school bus stop, etc.) will be furnished and installed at proper locations. Materials and installation for signs shall meet current Georgia Department of Transportation standards, and all expenses incurred will be borne by the developer at no cost to the city. Upon completion of sign installation, the city manager or his designee will inspect for compliance.
(b) All streets shall be designated by name on a street sign post approved by the building inspector or the city manager's designee with such post having a set of nameplates/planes of an approved material one above the other with a clearance of seven feet. The post shall be located to be visible for both pedestrian and vehicular traffic. At cross-street intersections in all zoning districts other than an R-1A, R-1B, or agricultural district, two street sign posts shall be located diagonally across the intersection from each other. Only one street sign post shall be required at T-street intersections.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
617:
Fire hydrants shall be distributed throughout any development such that every house must be within 500 feet of a hydrant. Fire protection shall be furnished for any developments connected to the public water supply system, and a minimum fire flow of 500 gpm for two hours shall be provided. 620:

The nature and duration of any arrangement requiring the documentation of improvement responsibilities and assurances shall be structured to achieve this goal without adding unnecessary costs to the developer.

621:
The city manager's designee shall administer this chapter. The city manager's designee shall have authority to adopt, with the approval of the mayor and council, procedures and specifications relating to the administration of these regulations and to the technical data required in these regulations. Said procedures and specifications, as hereinafter adopted or amended, shall be considered a part of these regulations. It shall be the duty of the city manager's designee to review sketch plans and to suggest changes which shall be made in the proposed design of a subdivision to ensure the approval of the sketch plans. It shall be the duty of the city manager's designee to review preliminary plats/plans and to approve or disapprove such plats/plans. It shall be the duty of the city manager's designee to review final plats and the information submitted with such final plats and to approve such final plats when the requirements of this chapter have been met and to disapprove such final plats when the requirements of this chapter have not been met. Final plats shall be forwarded to the mayor and city council for acceptance of dedications where applicable.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
622:
Before recording final subdivision plats/plans, and as a condition of final plat approval, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may approve and shall accept in accordance with the standards adopted by the chapter the following assurances:
(1) For a major subdivision, provisions for a maintenance assurance shall be made for a period not to exceed two years after the final acceptance of the improvement, in an amount equal to 25 percent of the cost of the improvements. In the event that other governmental agencies or public utilities will automatically own the utilities to be installed, or the improvements are covered by a performance or maintenance assurance to another governmental agency, no performance or maintenance assurance shall be required by the building inspector or the city manager's designee.
(2) Upon substantial completion of all required improvements, the developer shall notify the building inspector or the city manager's designee, in writing that such substantial completion has taken place. The building inspector or the city manager's designee, shall inspect all improvements to assure compliance with applicable standards. The building inspector or the city manager's designee shall file a report on the status of the affected improvements. If approved, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may notify the development party in writing that the specified improvements satisfy all applicable requirements. If only partially approved, or disapproved, the building inspector or the city manager's designee shall notify the developer in writing regarding any deficiencies concerning specified improvements and shall indicate any corrective action to be taken. Where partial approval is granted, the developer shall be released from all liability except for that portion of improvements not yet approved.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)
623:
Maintenance mechanism. At the time the city accepts and assumes ownership of the new streets, signs, drainage systems, or other public improvements, the developer shall be required to provide the city with security for the maintenance of the streets, signs, water system, sewer system, and drainage system for a period of two years commencing with the city's formal acceptance of same. The security shall be in the form of a surety bond, bank letter of credit, escrow account, or similar instrument that guarantees maintenance of the improvements and shall be in an amount equal to 25 percent of the cost of the improvements. Any surety bonds must be from a surety on the U.S. Department of Treasury's listing of approved sureties (Dept. Circular 570).
Extension of maintenance security for phased developments. For developments with multiple phases of construction, the building inspector or the city manager's designee may require that portions of a previously approved phase be placed under an extended maintenance bond or letter of credit if the previously approved phase is used as access for construction traffic for the development of future phases. The duration of such an extended maintenance bond or letter of credit shall not exceed three years from the date of approval of the final plat for the final phase of the development.
(Res. No. 24-10, att., 9-19-2023)

Sec. [54-]55-1. Short title.
This article shall be known as the City of Glennville Community Transportation Vehicle Ordinance.
Sec. [54-]55-2. Findings and intent.
This resolution is adopted to address the interest of public safety. Motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and other similar vehicles are not designed or manufactured to be used on public highways, streets and roads, (hereafter "public roads") and the City of Glennville in no way advocates their operation on the public roads within its jurisdiction. Adoption of this resolution is not to be relied upon as a determination by the City of Glennville that operation of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles on public roads is safe or advisable if done in accordance with this article. By regulating such operation the city is merely addressing safety issues. All persons who operate or ride in motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles on public roads do so with their own judgment and at their own risk, and must be observant of, and attentive to the safety of themselves and others, including their passengers, other motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, the City of Glennville has no liability in negligence, nuisance or under any other cause of action for losses resulting from the use of motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles on roads, sidewalks, rights-of-way or other public property under this article. Any person who operates motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles is responsible for procuring appropriate insurance as may be required by any State of Georgia law or this chapter as a condition of operating motorized carts, personal transportation vehicles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, low-speed vehicles, and other similar vehicles on the roads of the City of Glennville.
Sec. [54-]55-3. Definitions.
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the definitions respectively ascribed to them in this article.
All-terrain vehicle means any motorized vehicle designed for off-road use which is equipped with three or more low pressure tires and with a seat to be straddled by the operator and with handlebars for steering control. OR All-Terrain Vehicle shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(3).
Dealer means a person engaged in the business of buying, selling, or exchanging vehicles who has an established place of business in this state. OR Dealer shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(11).
Electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD) means a self-balancing, two nontandem wheeled device designed to transport only one person and having an electric propulsion system with average power of 750 watts (1 horsepower) and a maximum speed of less than 20 miles per hour on a paved level surface when powered solely by such propulsion system and ridden by an operator who weighs 170 pounds. OR Electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD) shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(15.6).
Gross weight means the unladen weight of the vehicle plus the weight of any load thereon.
Low-speed vehicle (LSV) means any four-wheeled electric vehicle whose top speed attainable in one mile is greater than 20 miles per hour but not greater than 25 miles per hour on a paved level surface and which is manufactured in compliance with those federal motor vehicle safety standards for low-speed vehicles set forth in 49 C.F.R. Section 571.500 and in effect on January 1, 2001. OR Low-Speed Vehicle (LSV) shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(25.1).
Motorized cart means every motor vehicle having no less than three wheels and an unladen weight on 1,300 pounds or less and which cannot operate at more than 20 miles per hours. OR Motorized cart shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(32).
Motor vehicle means every vehicle which is self-propelled other than an electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD). OR Motor Vehicle shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(33).
Personal transportation vehicle means any motor vehicle with a minimum of four wheels, capable of a maximum level ground speed of less than 20 miles per hour with a maximum gross vehicle unladen or empty weight of 1,375 pounds and capable of transporting not more than eight persons. The term does not include mobility aids, including power wheelchairs and scooters, which can be used indoors and outdoors for the express purpose of enabling mobility for a person with a disability. The term also does not include any all-terrain vehicle. OR Personal Transportation Vehicle shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(43.1).
Public road means the entire width between the boundary lines of every right-of-way or place open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular travel within the boundaries of the City of Glennville, including streets and alleys.
Sidewalk means that portion of public property of a street between the curb lines, or the lateral lines of a railway, and the adjacent property lines, intended for use only by pedestrians.
Unladen weight means the weight of a vehicle without load as per the manufacturer's specifications for such vehicle.
Valid motor vehicle driver's license means any current and valid certificate issued by the state, other state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits persons to operate motor vehicles on the public roads of the state.
Vehicle means every device in, upon, or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, excepting devices used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks. OR Vehicle shall have the same definition as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(75).
Sec. [54-]55-4. Nomenclature.
Any personal transportation vehicle, as defined by this chapter, which also qualifies as a motorized cart, as defined by this chapter, shall only be considered a motorized cart under this chapter and be subject only to the requirements, including registration, equipment, and inspections for motorized carts under this chapter.
Sec. [54-]55-5. Motorized cart registration.
(a) A fee of $15.00 to register each and every motorized cart for use on public roads will be charged by the City of Glennville to cover the costs of implementing and maintaining this article. It shall be the duty of every owner of a motorized cart that is operated on public roads, rights-of-way or other public property in the jurisdiction of the City of Glennville to register the motorized cart with the city within ten business days of the date of purchase. A grace period of 30 calendar days will be allowed for current owners of motorized carts upon adoption of this resolution.
(b) Registration with the City of Glennville shall include a record of the model, make, any vehicle identification number or serial number on such motorized cart, the name and address of the owner, a contact phone number, and any other such information as the city shall require, all of which shall be maintained by the Chief of Police, City of Glennville.
(c) Upon registration with the City of Glennville each motorized cart shall be issued a license decal from the city signifying such registration. The decals must be affixed to the driver's side of the motorized cart in such a manner as to be visible at all times and shall remain permanently with such motorized cart unless the motorized cart is sold or the license is destroyed.
(d) The failure to have a registration license decal affixed to a motorized cart for use on public roads, rights-of-way or other public property in the City of Glennville shall be a violation of this article and subject the owner of such motorized cart to the penalties set forth in section 1-11.
(e) If the motorized cart for use on public roads, rights-of-way or other public property is not registered with the city within ten business days of purchase it shall be considered and unregistered motorized cart and subject the owner of such motorized cart to penalties set forth in section 1-11. Furthermore, any motorized cart for use on public roads not registered within ten business days of purchase shall be assessed a late registration fee of $30.00.
(f) The decal issued by the city shall be non-transferrable from the motorized cart for which is it was obtained.
(g) Upon transfer of the motorized cart to the ownership of another person, the registration must be transferred to the new owner within ten business days of the change in ownership at a cost of $15.00. If the registration is not transferred within ten business days it shall be considered and unregistered motorized cart and subject the owner of such motorized cart to penalties set forth in section 1-11. Furthermore, any motorized cart for use on public roads not registered within ten business days of purchase shall be assessed a late registration fee of $30.00.
(h) Motorized cart dealers and distributors, along with other commercial establishments, may rent motorized carts to the public for use on designated public roads, rights-of-way or other public property. Each such establishment renting motorized carts shall be required to register each such motorized cart in accordance with this section and shall maintain a written record of each person who rents each cart. Renters shall be required to furnish positive identification, shall be provided a copy of this article to read, and must be at least 16 years of age. The registration fee and transfer fees and regulations, along with all licensing and operation regulations shall be consistent with the provisions of this article as pertains to motorized carts.
(i) Only those persons 18 years of age and older may register a motorized cart. Motorized cart registration may be in one person's name only, and the registration form must be signed by that person.
(j) Any owner or operator registering a motorized cart with the city agrees to abide by all of the requirements of state law and this code. By registering a motorized cart with the city the owner or operator verifies that the vehicle qualifies to be classified as such under state law and this code.
(k) The city council may, at its discretion, and by resolution, waive registration requirements for special events of a limited duration to which out-of-city residents may bring motorized carts as participants. Such special events shall last no longer than seven calendar days.
Sec. [54-]55-6. Personal transportation vehicle equipment and inspections.
(a) All personal transportation vehicles shall have a braking system sufficient for the weight and passenger capacity of the vehicle including a parking brake, a reverse warning device functional at all times when the directional control is in the reverse position, a main power switch which shall render the power circuit inoperative when the switch is in the ‘off’ position or the key or other activating device is removed, such key or other activating device only being removable in the ‘off’ position, head lamps, reflex reflectors, tail lamps, a horn, a rearview mirror, safety warning labels, and hip restraints and hand holds.
(b) All personal transportation vehicles which do not also qualify as motorized carts shall comply with all applicable provisions of Article 1, Chapter 8, Title 40 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.
Sec. [54-]55-7. Personal transportation and low-speed vehicle registration.
(a) Any personal transportation vehicle which does not also qualify as a motorized cart, low-speed vehicle, or other motor vehicle required to be registered by Georgia law shall register such motor vehicle with the State of Georgia, as required by law, before being allowed to operate within the boundaries of the City of Glennville.
(b) Only registered personal transportation vehicles may be operated on designated public property within the boundaries of the city, subject to limitations provided in this article.
Sec. [54-]55-8. Motorized cart operation regulations.
(a) Motorized carts may only be driven on designated public roads, rights-of-way or other public property of the city.
(1) The designated public roads shall include all public roads within the jurisdiction of the city (excluding US 25/301; GA 23/144,) which have a speed limit of 35 miles per hour or less.
Note: GA Highway 23/144 from the intersection of Tillman and Barnard Street to the intersection of Church and Barnard Street shall be considered designated public road for travel of motorized carts.
(2) Designated rights-of-way or other public property includes all public rights-of-way and public property of the city.
(b) Motorized carts shall not be operated on sidewalks at any time with the exception of:
(1) Residents of Lakeview may travel on the sidewalk East side of US 301/25 from Oliver Lane to Banks Street.
(2) Residents of Deloach Lane and Camelot Subdivision may travel on the sidewalk West of US 301/25 from Deloach Lane to Gordon Street.
(c) No person shall operate a motorized cart on a public road of the City of Glennville unless that road is designated for motorized cart use by this article. The city shall post appropriate signs directing motorized carts and other explicitly allowed vehicles to cross only at designated crossings.
(d) No motorized cart may cross any street, road or highway which is part of US Highway 301/25 (Veterans Boulevard) or State Highway 23/144 (Barnard Street) with the exception of the below listed crossings.
(1) Intersection of US 301/25 and Barnard Street (traffic light).
(2) Intersection of GA 144 (Barnard Street) and Tillman Street.
(3) Intersection of GA 144/23 (Barnard Street) and Church Street.
(e) Motorized carts may cross streets, roads and highways which are part of the City of Glennville street system only at crossings or intersections as outlined in (d) above.
(f) Motorized carts may only be operated on public roads, rights-of-way or other public property which are part of the City of Glennville street system during daylight hours unless the motorized cart complies with equipment regulations which may be promulgated by the Commissioner of Public Safety of the State of Georgia.
(g) Motorized cart owners shall maintain their motorized carts in a manner which ensures that an unobstructed view from the driver's seat to the rear is maintained at all times the motorized cart is in operation on public roads.
(h) The maximum occupancy of a motorized cart traveling on public roads, sidewalks, paths, rights-of-way or other public property shall be one person per designated seat.
(i) All operators of motorized carts shall abide by all traffic regulations applicable to vehicular traffic when using the designated public roads, rights-of-way or other public property of the city.
Sec. [54-]55-9. Personal transportation vehicle, low-speed vehicle and all-terrain vehicle operation regulations.
(a) Only personal transportation vehicles which also qualify as a motorized cart may be operated on the public roads within the territorial boundaries of the city. Such personal transportation vehicles must comply with all of the requirements for motorized carts under state law and this article.
(b) Low-speed vehicles shall not be operated on sidewalks at any time.
(c) All operators shall abide by all traffic regulations applicable to vehicular traffic when using the designated public roads, sidewalks, paths, rights-of-way or other property accessible to the public in the city.
(d) Low-speed vehicle being operated on the highways of the state, including city roads and rights of way, shall display an amber strobe light which shall be visible under normal atmospheric conditions from a distance of 500 feet from the front and rear of such vehicle.
(e) No low-speed vehicle shall be permitted to operate on any public and State road within the territorial boundaries of the city where the posted speed limit exceeds 35 miles per hour. Except as prohibited by law, low-speed vehicles shall be permitted to cross over streets of which the posted speed limit exceeds 35 miles per hour as long as the low-speed vehicle is traveling from one street with a posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour or less to another street with a posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour or less.
(f) No all-terrain vehicle shall be permitted to operate on any public roads, sidewalks, paths, rights-of-way or other public property of the city. Violations will be prosecuted under the Code of Georgia, Title 40, Chapter 7, pertaining to "off-road vehicles".
Sec. [54-]55-10. Gasoline-powered motorized carts and personal transportation vehicles.
(a) Every gasoline-powered motorized cart and personal transportation vehicle shall at all times be equipped with an exhaust system in good working order and in constant operation, meeting the following specifications:
(1) The exhaust system shall include the piping leading from the flange of the exhaust manifold to and including the muffler and exhaust pipes or include any and all parts specified by the manufacturer.
(2) The exhaust system in its own shall be securely fastened, including the consideration of missing or broken brackets or hangers.
(3) The engine and power mechanism of every gasoline-powered motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle shall be so equipped, adjusted, and tuned, as to prevent the escape of excessive smoke or fumes.
(b) It shall be unlawful for the owner of any gasoline-powered motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle to operate or permit the operation of such gasoline-powered motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle on which any device controlling or abating atmospheric conditions, which is placed on the gasoline-powered motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle by the manufacturer, to render the device unserviceable by removal, alteration, or other interference with its operation.
(c) All gasoline-powered motorized carts or personal transportation vehicles shall be maintained in working order and kept in good condition and shall be subject to inspection by city officials at reasonable times and intervals.
(d) All gasoline-powered motorized carts or personal transportation vehicles shall be maintained in such condition so that they are incapable of "backfiring", or otherwise operating so as to make loud noises; or create noise as a result of an operators equipping the gasoline-powered motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle with a certain device.
Sec. [54-]55-11. Motorized cart operator licensing regulations.
(a) Those persons possessing a valid motor vehicle driver's license issued by the state, other state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits such person to operate a motor vehicle on the highways of the state may operate and drive a motorized cart on designated public roads, rights-of-way or other permitted public property of the city.
(b) Those persons who are 15 years of age but not yet 16 years of age may drive a motorized cart if he/she holds a valid instructional permit issued by the state pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 40-5-24, as may be amended, and he/she is accompanied in the front seat by a person at least 18 years of age who holds a valid motor vehicle driver's license.
(c) Those persons who are 12 years of age but not yet 15 years of age may drive a motorized cart on the designated streets if they are accompanied in the front seat by a parent, grandparent or legal guardian which holds a valid motor vehicle license.
Sec. [54-]55-12. Personal transportation and low-speed vehicle operator licensing regulations.
Only those persons possessing a valid motor vehicle driver's license issued by the state, other state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits such person to operate a motor vehicle on the public roads of the state may operate a personal transportation vehicle or low-speed vehicle on the public roads within the territorial boundaries of the city.
(a) Those persons who are 15 years of age but not yet 16 years of age may drive a personal transportation or low speed vehicle if he/she holds a valid instructional permit issued by the state pursuant to O.C. G. A. § 40-5-24, as may be amended, and he/she is accompanied in the front seat by a person at least 18 years of age who holds a valid motor vehicle driver's license.
(b) Those persons who are 12 years of age but not yet 15 years of age may drive a personal transportation or low speed vehicle on the designated streets if they are accompanied in the front seat by a parent, grandparent or legal guardian.
Sec. [54-]55-13. Insurance.
(a) The owner or operator of a motorized cart is liable for his or her own actions. Any person who operates or owns a motorized cart is responsible for procuring liability insurance and verifying coverage in terms enough to cover risk involved in using such motorized cart on designated public roads, rights-of-way or other public property of the city.
(b) The owner or operator of a personal transportation vehicle which does not also qualify as a motorized cart shall keep proof or evidence of required minimum insurance coverage in the personal transportation vehicle at all times during the operation of the motor vehicle as required by state law.
(c) The owner or operator of a low speed vehicle shall keep proof or evidence of required minimum insurance coverage in the low speed vehicle at all times during the operation of the motor vehicle as required by state law.
Sec [54-]55-14. Hazardous activities and special rules.
(a) Blocking of public access to any public roads, sidewalks, recreation paths, rights-of-way or other public property of the city shall be prohibited, except for permitted events.
(b) All operators and passengers of motorized carts, low-speed vehicles, personal transportation vehicles, and other motor vehicles shall remain seated at all times during the operation of motor vehicle.
Sec. [54-]55-15. Penalties.
(a) Any person who violates the terms of this article shall be cited to appear before the municipal court or other court of appropriate jurisdiction and, upon conviction, punished as provided in the Code of Glennville, Georgia.
(b) In addition to enforcing sanctions against the operator, any violation of this article shall be charged against the registered owner of the vehicle, and all fines and penalties shall be levied against the registered owner of the vehicle as follows:
(1) For the first offense, warning.
(2) For the second offense committed within one year of conviction for a first offense, a fine of not to exceed $50.00; and
(3) For a third offense committed within one year of conviction for a second offense for a vehicle, a fine of not to exceed $100.00, and if a motorized cart the registered owner's motorized cart city registration shall be revoked. The registered owner cannot thereafter register a motorized cart for use in the city for a period of two years following the third conviction. Additionally, such person shall be prohibited from operating a motorized cart or personal transportation vehicle on the public roads, rights-of-way, or other public property for a period of two years.
(c) Any violation by an operator of a low-speed vehicle shall be charged against the operator according to the provisions of Title 40 of the Official Code of Georgia and this Code. Any violation by an owner of a low-speed vehicle shall be charged against the owner according to the provisions of Title 40 of the Official Code of Georgia and this Code.
(d) Any violation by and operator of a personal transportation vehicle, EPAMD, or other motor vehicle may be charged against the operator according to this Code or according to the provisions of Title 40 of the Official Code of Georgia.

All meters, curb cocks, valves, meter boxes and fire hydrants connected with the city water mains and service pipes, including those furnished at the expense of consumers or property owners, shall remain under the direct control of the water and fire department and it shall be unlawful for persons other than those authorized by the city to connect, disconnect or tamper with any such meter, or to turn off the water at the curb cock, valve or meter, or to open, move or tamper with any meter box, to tamper or turn on any fire hydrant. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere or in any way meddle with any of the wells, reservoirs, conduits, basins or with the water in the same, or to make or knowingly permit any connection or tapping on his premises, except as authorized by this chapter.
(Code 1982, 14-111; Ord. No. 08-09, 8-7-2007)

No more than one building shall be permitted to use a water service line. Only galvanized pipe or PVC shall be used for the installation of a service line and all service lines shall be installed at a depth of at least 12 inches below the surface of the ground. Each service line shall contain a stop and waste cock where the water may be turned off.
(Code 1982, § 14-113)
865:
Consumers shall prevent unnecessary waste of water and keep all water outlets closed when not in actual use. Hydrants, urinals, water closets, bath tubs and other fixtures must not be left running for any purpose other than the use for which they were intended. When any such waste occurs, the water service may be terminated.
(Code 1982, § 14-114)
866:
During all fire alarms the use by persons other than municipal firefighters of hoses and other apparatuses maintaining a constant flow of water is absolutely forbidden.
(Code 1982, § 14-116)
867:
(a) Water meters shall be read on the 20th day of each month, as nearly as possible, and bills shall be mailed on the first day of each succeeding month. All water bills shall be due on or before the tenth day of the month following the reading of the meter, and if not paid by the twentieth, a penalty (which is on file in the city clerk's office) shall be added thereto and paid by the water user.
(b) In the event of nonpayment and service cut off, the customer must pay the bill in full, the late payment charge, a cut off charge if applicable, and pay a deposit if it was either waived, previously refunded, or was used to make the payment, late payment charge, and/or the cut-off charge.
(c) When unforeseen circumstances occur such as water leaks resulting in excessive high utility cost, the city manager or her designee is authorized to work out a payment plan for customers that demonstrate the ability to pay, but in no event shall such payment plan exceed 90 days before the customer's account is totally current. Such a payment plan can only be entered into once in a 12-month period. Failure to meet any payment date of a payment plan shall terminate the payment plan, and the services shall be discontinued.
(d) The city manager or designee shall be authorized to make equitable adjustments in billing for wastewater services only in cases where leaks in pipes and plumbing facilities result in increased billings without fault on the part of the customer. Such adjustments shall be made based on an average of prior billings only after repairs have been made and certified by a licensed plumber, and shall be limited to two months' billings.
(e) Failure to receive water/wastewater billing does not relieve the customer from obligation. It shall be the customer's responsibility to check all the charges on the bill. If the customer is charged for any services not received, the city manager or designee shall adjust the charges for up to three months. Further, if the customer is receiving unauthorized services for which they are not being billed, the city manager or designee will adjust their bill for no more than three months.
(Code 1982, § 14-118; Ord. No. 08-39, 3-11-2008; Res. No. 14-06, 9-3-2013)
868:
If any bill for water as hereinabove provided is not paid within ten days of the due date, the water service may be cut off, and in no case shall it be reinstated to the same property until the delinquencies shall have been paid in full.
(Code 1982, § 14-119; Amd. of 7-6-2006)
869:

(b) When the water supply is requested to be turned on for the purpose of cleaning vacant premises, one month trash pickup will be included in the cost. A charge on file in the clerk's office shall be made for temporary water service.
(c) Requests for water to remain on while premises are vacant, customer will only be charged for water/sewer; garbage costs will be omitted while premises are vacant. A charge on file in the clerk's office shall be made for continued water service.
(d) When water supply is requested, and the requestor has outstanding water, sewer and garbage fees on file from a previous account, the outstanding amount must be paid in full. In addition the requestor must pay a deposit of two times the normal water/sewer deposit fee plus an application fee and any other standard fees before receiving new services. The normal water deposit fee is on file in the clerk's office.
(Code 1982, § 14-120; Ord. No. 08-35, 2-5-2008; Res. No. 12-32, 6-5-2012)
870:
(a) Title and purpose. This section shall be known as the "Private Well Drilling Ordinance." The purpose of this section is to prohibit the drilling of private wells (except those for irrigation purposes) within the corporate city limits of the city; to require that all new construction requiring water service to be connected to the city water system; to prohibit the connection of any water system supplied by a private well to the water system of the city; to provide penalties for violating this section; and to insure the provision of a safe and sanitary drinking water supply.

City means City of Glennville.
City Code means City of Glennville Code of Ordinances.
Department means City of Glennville Water Department.
Well means any means of drawing ground water for use or consumption.
(c) Offenses declared. Any violation of this section shall be punished as provide in section 58-58 of this Code. All new construction to be occupied as homes, residences, business, etc., shall be connected with the city water system. It shall be unlawful for any owner to allow a house or business to be occupied or for any tenant to occupy a house or business unless the same is connected with the city water system.

Any and all houses, homes and/or businesses that are connected to an existing well at the time of this section may remain on those wells until such time the wells are declared unserviceable; at which time the home, house and/or business shall be connected to the city water system.

871:

872:

875:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Auxiliary intake means any piping connection or other device whereby water may be secured from a source other than that normally used.
Bypass means any system of piping or other arrangement whereby the water may be diverted around any part or portion of a water purification plant.
Cross connection means any physical connection whereby the public water supply is connected with any other water supply system, whether public or private, either inside or outside of any building or buildings, in such manner that a flow of water into the public water supply is possible either through the manipulation of valves or because of ineffective check or back pressure valves, or because of any other arrangement.
Interconnection means any system of piping or other arrangement whereby the public water supply is connected directly with a sewer, drain, conduit, pool, storage reservoir, or other device which does or may contain sewage or other waste or liquid which would be capable of imparting contamination to the public water supply.
Person means any and all persons, natural or artificial, including any individual firm or association, and any municipal or private corporation organized or existing under the laws of this state or any other state or county.
Public water supply means the waterworks system furnishing water to the city for general use and which supply is recognized as the public water supply by the state department of natural resources/environmental protection division.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 1)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
876:
The city public water supply shall comply with chapter 391-3-5-.13 of the Georgia Rules for Safe Drinking Water and PL 93-523 of the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act, legally adopted in accordance with this chapter, which pertain to cross connections, and establish an effective, ongoing program to control these undesirable water uses.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 2)
877:
It shall be unlawful for any person to cause a cross connection, auxiliary intake, bypass or interconnection to be made; or allow one to exist for any purpose whatsoever.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 3)
878:
Any person whose premises are supplied with water from the public water supply, and who also has on the same premises a separate source of water supply or stores water in an uncovered or unsanitary storage reservoir from which the water stored therein is circulated through a piping system, shall file with the clerk a statement of the non-existence of unapproved or unauthorized cross connections, auxiliary intakes, bypasses or interconnections. Such statement shall also contain an agreement that no cross connection, auxiliary intake, bypass or interconnection will be permitted upon the premises.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 4)
879:
It shall be the duty of the city public water supply to cause inspections to be made of all properties served by the public water supply where cross connections with the public water supply are deemed possible. The frequency of inspections and reinspections based on potential health hazards involved shall be as established by the mayor and council.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 5)
880:
The water superintendent or authorized representative shall have the right to enter at any reasonable time, any property served by a connection to the city public water supply for the purpose of inspecting the piping systems thereof for cross connections, auxiliary intakes, bypasses or interconnection. On request, the owner, lessee or occupant of any property so served shall furnish to the inspection agency any pertinent information regarding the piping system or systems on such property. The refusal of such information or refusal of access, when requested, shall be deemed evidence of the presence of cross connections.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 6)
882:
The potable water supply made available on the properties served by the public water supply shall be protected from possible contamination as specified herein. Any water outlet which could be used for potable or domestic purposes and which is not supplied by the potable system must be labeled in a conspicuous manner as:
WATER UNSAFE FOR DRINKING
The minimum acceptable sign shall have black letters one inch high located on a red background.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 9)
883:
Any person who neglects or refuses to comply with any of the provisions of this article shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction therefor, shall be subject to section 1-11. Each day of continued violation after conviction shall constitute a separate offense. In addition to the foregoing fines and penalties, the city shall discontinue the public water supply service at any premises upon which there is found to be a cross connection, auxiliary intake, bypass or interconnection, and service shall not be restored until such cross connection, auxiliary intake, bypass or interconnection has been discontinued.
(Ord. of 7-11-1989, § 10)

888:
These rules apply to any entity, and its customers, permitted by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) for water withdrawal or for operation of a drinking water system.
(Res. No. 11-12, 12-7-2010)
889:
(a) Outdoor water use other than exempted activities shall occur only as follows:
(1) Odd-numbered addresses: outdoor water use in allowed on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.
(2) Even-numbered addresses: outdoor water use is allowed on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays.
(Res. No. 11-12, 12-7-2010)
890:
(a) The director of the environmental protection division is authorized to make drought declarations.
(b) During declared drought conditions, outdoor water use other than activities exempted in 58-135 shall occur only during scheduled hours on the scheduled days.
(c) Declared Drought Response Level One—Outdoor water use may occur on scheduled days within the hours of 12:00 midnight to 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight.
(1) Scheduled days for off-numbered addresses are Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.
(2) Scheduled days for even-numbered addresses are Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays.
(3) Use of hydrants for any purpose other than firefighting, public health, safety or flushing is prohibited.
(d) Declared Drought Response Level Two—Outdoor watering use may occur on scheduled days within the hours of 12:00 midnight to 10:00a.m.
(1) Scheduled days for odd-numbered addresses are Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.
(2) Scheduled days for even-numbered addresses and golf course fairways are Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays.
(3) The following uses are prohibited:
a. Using hydrants for any purpose other than firefighting, public health, safety or flushing.
b. Washing hard surfaces, such as streets, gutters, sidewalks and driveways except when necessary for public safety.
(e) Declared Drought Response Level Three—Outdoor water use may occur on the scheduled day within the hours of 12:00 midnight to 10:00 a.m.
(1) The scheduled day for odd-numbered addresses is Sunday.
(2) The scheduled day for even-numbered addresses and golf course fairways is Saturday.
(3) The following uses are prohibited:
a. Using hydrants for any purpose other than firefighting, public health, safety or flushing.
b. Washing hard surfaces, such as streets, gutters, sidewalks, driveways, except when necessary for public health and safety.
c. Filing installed swimming pools except when necessary for health care or structural integrity.
d. Washing vehicles, such as cars, boats, trailers, motorbikes, airplanes, golf carts.
e. Washing buildings or structures except for immediate fire protection.
f. Non-commercial fund-raisers, such as car washes.
g. Using water for ornamental purposes, such as fountains, reflecting pools, and waterfalls except when necessary to support aquatic life.
(f) Declared Drought Response Level Four—No outdoor water use is allowed, other than for activities exempted in section 58-135, or as the EPD director may order.
(Res. No. 11-12, 12-7-2010)
891:
(a) This rule shall not apply to the following outdoor water uses:
(1) Captured and re-use of cooling system condensate or storm water in compliance with applicable local ordinances.
(2) Re-use of gray water in compliance with applicable local ordinances.

(1) Use of reclaimed wastewater by a designated user from a system permitted by EPD to provide reclaimed wastewater.
(2) Irrigation of personal food gardens.

(2) For new landscapes installed by certified or licensed professionals, commercial exemptions apply.
(d) The following golf course outdoor water uses are exempt from the outdoor water use schedules of this rule.
(1) Use of reclaimed wastewater by a designated user fom a system permitted by EPD to provide reclaimed wastewater.
(2) Irrigation of fairways during times of non-drought and Declared Drought Response Level One.
(3) Irrigation of tees during times of non-drought and Declared Drought Response Levels One, Two and Three.
(4) Irrigation of greens.
(e) The following commercial outdoor water uses are exempt from the outdoor water use schedules of this rule.
(1) Professionally certified or licensed landscapers, golf course contractors, and sports turf landscapers: During installation and 30 days following installation only. Professional landscapers must be certified or licensed for commercial exemptions to apply.
(2) Irrigation contractors: During installation and as needed for proper maintenance and adjustment only.
(3) Sod producers.
(4) Ornamental growers.
(5) Fruit and vegetable growers.
(6) Retail garden centers.
(7) Hydro-seeding.
(8) Power washing.
(9) Construction sites.
(10) Producers of food and fiber.
(11) Car washes.
(12) Other activities essential to daily business.
(13) Watering-in of pesticides and herbicides on turf.
(Res. No. 11-12, 12-7-2010)
892:
Enforcement actions shall be taken on those users not complying with this article in the manner described in this article.

893:
Duly authorized officers bearing proper credentials and identification shall be permitted to enter all properties with the purpose of inspection, observation, measurement and testing in accordance with the provisions of this article.

894:

(c) Subsequent violations. All subsequent violations shall be charged a reconnection fee of $200.00 for each violation.

897:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Commercial means any type of building other than residential.
Construction means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and shall include the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, shower head, toilet, or urinal in an existing building.
Residential means any building or unit of a building intended for occupancy as dwelling but shall not include a hotel or motel.
(Ord. No. 01-24, § 2(1), 6-5-2001)
